title: PageSpeed / web-performance report — ONE ROUND
description: One file = ONE round of the PageSpeed report (one 4-column block in the Sheet). A round is a set of scores collected for the SAME pages, on the SAME platforms, in the SAME environment, with the SAME tool — that quadruple is the identity of the numbers. Comparing a score across a different env/profile/tool is a category error, not a regression. HONESTY CONTRACT (the validator can only check shape; the RULES and the tools enforce the rest): (1) status 'measured' REQUIRES `score` AND `runs`, and requires runs.length === source.runsPerPage — a page whose successful runs fell below the target is 'not-run', never a partial green number; psi-run.mjs and psi-sheet.mjs enforce this, the schema cannot (no conditional keywords in the kit's validator subset). (2) 0 is a REAL score — an absent measurement is 'not-run' (temporary) or 'n-a' (the page does not exist on that platform/round) or 'error' (the tool failed), and NEVER 0. (3) A score is a LAB metric from a single load and a single load is noise: the cell carries the MEDIAN of `runs` and every individual run is kept. (4) A metric with no `budgets` block is REPORTED, never JUDGED — Google's 90/50 colour bands are a classification, not a pass/fail line; a verdict needs owner-approved budgets (approvedBy + approvedOn). Raising a budget to make the report green is fabrication. (5) Lab (Lighthouse/PSI) is not field (CrUX): `metrics` is lab, `field` is real users — never present one as the other.

round.description: Identity of this round. env is part of the identity of every number in it.

id.description: Slug used as the file name: rounds/<id>.json. e.g. 'r6', '2026-06-05-prod'.

date.description: The date the round was collected (YYYY-MM-DD).

env.description: Where the pages were measured. A staging number and a production number are NOT comparable: a regression is same page + same platform + same env + same profile + same tool.

label.description: The header text of this round's block in the Sheet, verbatim — e.g. 'Points from 05/06/2024 (Prod)'.

source.description: How the numbers were produced. Two rounds collected with different tools/profiles are not comparable, so this travels with the data.

tool.description: psi-api = the PageSpeed Insights API (Google's servers, needs an API key). pagespeed-web = a human pasting URLs into pagespeed.web.dev. lighthouse-cli = a LOCAL Lighthouse run — local numbers depend on the machine and are NOT comparable with PSI numbers. One round = one tool; never mix engines inside a round.

lighthouseVersion.description: e.g. '11.0.0'. Lighthouse changes its scoring weights between major versions: a score jump across versions is a TOOL change, not a product change. Record it or you cannot tell the difference later.

runsPerPage.description: The target number of runs per page per platform. Default 3 — a single load is noise. `runs` shorter than this means the target was NOT met, and the result must be 'not-run'.

strategyProfiles.description: Which platform profiles this round covers. A platform absent here has no rows in this round's block.

collectedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the collection run.

budgets.description: OPTIONAL — and its absence is the point: with NO budgets block, this report REPORTS numbers and never judges them. A budget is what makes a pass/fail verdict possible, and a budget only exists once a human owner approved it (approvedBy + approvedOn). Changing a budget so a red number turns green is FABRICATION — the same rule as re-baselining a visual-regression golden to hide a diff.

lcpMs.description: Maximum acceptable Largest Contentful Paint, ms.

tbtMs.description: Maximum acceptable Total Blocking Time, ms.

inpMs.description: Maximum acceptable Interaction to Next Paint, ms (FIELD metric — only judgeable against `field`, not against lab `metrics`).

approvedBy.description: The human who approved these numbers as the line. An agent may PROPOSE a budget; it may never approve one.

approvedOn.description: When it was approved (YYYY-MM-DD). A budget with no date has no history — and a budget with no history can be quietly loosened.

pages.description: One entry per page in the report; each carries one result per platform. A round with no pages is not a round.

id.description: Stable page key. The Sheet carries rounds over BY (page id, platform), so renaming an id orphans its history — treat it as permanent.

name.description: Human name shown in column A of the Sheet (hyperlinked to url).

url.description: The exact URL measured, including the env's host. Two rounds on the same page id with different hosts are different environments — see round.env.

section.description: Section band the page sits under in the Sheet (e.g. 'Consumer site Pages').

results.description: One result per platform for this page in this round.

status.description: measured = the target run count succeeded; REQUIRES score + runs (enforced by psi-run.mjs / psi-sheet.mjs — the validator subset has no conditional keywords). not-run = not run this round, or fewer successful runs than source.runsPerPage → EMPTY cell, never a number. n-a = the page does not exist on this platform / in this round → comment MANDATORY. error = the tool failed → comment MANDATORY. Nothing here is ever recorded as 0.

score.description: The Performance score written into the Sheet cell: the MEDIAN of `runs`, not an average and not the best run. 0 is a real score (a page that scored 0 genuinely scored 0); a MISSING measurement is 'not-run'/'n-a'/'error' — never 0. Only status 'measured' may carry a score.

runs.description: Every individual run's score, in collection order. Kept so the spread is visible: 91/58/89 is not 'the page scores 89', it is an unstable page, and the median hides that unless the runs travel with it.

metrics.description: LAB metrics of the MEDIAN run (the same run the score came from — mixing the median score with another run's metrics describes a load that never happened). The score never explains itself: '73' alone tells nobody what regressed, so LCP/TBT/CLS ride with it into the cell note.

inpMs.description: Interaction to Next Paint, ms — lab INP is an estimate; the real one is a FIELD metric (see `field`).

field.description: CrUX FIELD data (real users, 28-day window) when Google has it for this URL/origin. Lab != field: never present a lab number as user experience, and never present the absence of field data as a good result. ABSENT field data means Google has no sample — it does NOT mean zero.

source.description: crux-url = the sample is for THIS URL. crux-origin = Google had no URL-level sample and fell back to the whole origin — that number describes the site, not this page. Recording which one it was is the difference between evidence and a guess.

comment.description: The Comments cell (merged across the page's 2 rows in the Sheet). MANDATORY when: score < 50 · the score dropped >= 10 points vs the previous round in the SAME env · the page did not return 200 / rendered an empty state · the run count fell below source.runsPerPage · status is 'n-a' or 'error'. psi-run.mjs writes a 'NEEDS-COMMENT: …' placeholder when a comment is mandatory but only a human can write it — that string is a DEMAND, not an explanation, and a round still carrying one is not publishable.

collectedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the median run for this page+platform.

error.description: Verbatim failure text when status is 'error' (or the last failure when a partial 'not-run' had failures). The error is the evidence that the cell is empty for a reason.

evidence.description: The report behind the number. It is written by psi-report.mjs, and it may ONLY ever describe the MEDIAN run of THIS result — the run whose score is in `score`. That is the whole point: a link to a report of a different run (a fresh pagespeed.web.dev analysis, yesterday's run, the best of three) is evidence of something else, and the Sheet would then show a number the report contradicts. `runScore` is REQUIRED: it is the mismatch guard's anchor (psi-sheet.mjs refuses to publish when it disagrees with `score`), and an evidence block without it is an unauditable link — deleting it must make the round INVALID, not merely silence the guard. Note that a pagespeed.web.dev /analysis/<id> URL is deliberately not a field here: it expires in 30 days and dies with the host (PAGESPEED_REPORT_RULES rule 16).

reportUrl.description: The rendered Lighthouse report of the median run — the Sheet's Platform cell (Desktop / Mobile) links here. Self-hosted (Mega / Drive / the HTML-Reports publisher), so it outlives the 30-day PSI link.

screenshotUrl.description: Full-page PNG of that same report, for people who want the picture rather than the page.

runScore.description: The score shown IN the linked report. psi-sheet.mjs refuses to publish when this disagrees with `score` — that mismatch means the evidence belongs to a different run, which is exactly the failure this field exists to catch.

capturedAt.description: When the report was rendered from the stored Lighthouse result (not when the page was measured — that is `collectedAt`).
